content.value_statement: Frontend tasks often span components, state, routes, tests, and documentation. This skill organizes that work into clear context packages and quality checks.
actual_capabilities: Maps frontend work across components, routes, state, tests, and documentation.
Packages task context for related React, state, route, style, and test skills.
Defines validation checks for rendering, responsiveness, keyboard access, and screen reader support.
Tracks integration points with backend API changes and documentation updates.
Sets success metrics for visual tests, accessibility, performance, TypeScript, and component reuse.
limitations: Does not include executable scripts or automation files.
Depends on other frontend skills for actual component, routing, style, and test implementation.
Assumes React, TypeScript, Tailwind, Playwright, and related project conventions.
Does not replace manual review of UI behavior, API contracts, or accessibility results.

use_cases.title: Plan a UI feature
use_cases.description: Break a new interface request into components, state needs, routes, tests, and documentation updates.

use_cases.title: Coordinate API-driven UI changes
use_cases.description: Align frontend tasks with backend contract updates, loading states, error formats, and release checks.

use_cases.title: Prepare release quality checks
use_cases.description: Define visual, accessibility, responsive, performance, and TypeScript checks before frontend release.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a React component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-orchestrator to plan a new React component. Include responsibilities, state needs, routes, tests, and documentation updates.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate state and routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-orchestrator for a feature that changes state and routing. Identify affected components, actions, selectors, routes, and test coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Handle an API contract change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-orchestrator to coordinate a backend API change. Cover error formats, loading states, component updates, tests, and docs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a frontend release workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-orchestrator to review a release plan. Check visual, accessibility, responsive, performance, TypeScript, and component reuse requirements.

output_examples.input: Plan a password reset form for an auth route.
output_examples.output: A frontend task plan listing target components, route changes, auth state updates, validation states, visual checks, and documentation updates.

output_examples.input: Coordinate a backend response format change for login errors.
output_examples.output: An integration plan covering error display behavior, affected components, state updates, accessibility checks, and release validation tasks.

output_examples.input: Review readiness for a responsive dashboard release.
output_examples.output: A quality checklist for viewport coverage, visual tests, accessibility, performance targets, TypeScript status, and component reuse.

best_practices: Provide the target feature, affected route, existing components, and expected user states.
Ask for accessibility, responsive, visual, unit, and integration checks in the same request.
Keep backend contract changes and documentation updates visible in the task context.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to skip implementation review or visual test inspection.
Do not assign broad frontend work without naming affected components or routes.
Do not ignore accessibility, loading, error, and responsive states.

faq.question: What projects does this skill fit?
faq.answer: It fits React and TypeScript frontend projects that use organized components, state, routes, tests, and documentation.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill file provides planning guidance and quality checks, not executable scripts or command wrappers.

faq.question: Can it implement components directly?
faq.answer: It coordinates component work and delegates details to related frontend skills or the active coding agent.

faq.question: Does it cover accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It calls for WCAG AA review, keyboard navigation, screen reader support, and responsive checks.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What should I provide in a prompt?
faq.answer: Provide the feature goal, affected files or routes, existing components, API changes, and required quality checks.
